en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śramaṇa Yijing under Imperial Commission.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was staying in the city of Śrāvastī, at the Jetavana Grove.
At the Anāthapiṇḍada Monastery,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
and twelve thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, in the assembly at the Sudharmā Hall of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
there was a son of heaven named Sunetra, who,
together with various great devas and celestial maidens, [was present].
Surrounded by their retinues before and behind, they receive supreme honor and nobility;
they enjoy various celestial pleasures through joyful play and amuse themselves together, experiencing all manner of bliss.
At that time, during the night, the Devaputra Susthita heard a voice saying:
"The Devaputra Susthita shall certainly meet his death seven days from now."
After passing away from this life, he was reborn in Jambudvīpa,
where he underwent the bodies of animals for seven successive lifetimes;
subsequently, he experienced the sufferings of hell and emerged from it.
Having fortunately obtained a human body, he was born into a poor and lowly family;
while still in his mother’s womb, he was born without both eyes.
When the Devaputra Sunihita heard these words, he...
The hairs on his body all stood on end as he was seized by great terror;
filled with grief and distress, and overwhelmed by panic, he knew not what to do,
so he immediately hurried to the abode of Śakra, Lord of the Devas.
Wailing and weeping with grief,
they prostrated at the feet of the Lord of Devas, the Honored One of Two Legs, and addressed Śakra, saying:
"We pray that the Celestial Honored One will listen to what we have to say."
While I was surrounded by celestial maidens and experiencing pleasure, I heard a voice say:
"The life of the Devaputra Sunetra will come to an end in seven days."
After his life ended, he was reborn in Jambudvīpa; thereupon,
he underwent the bodies of animals for seven successive lifetimes,
followed by the suffering of hell, from which he eventually emerged.
"I had hoped to obtain a human body, yet I was born into a poor and lowly family;
while still in my mother's womb, I lost both eyes.
Hearing these words, I was struck with terror and at a loss for what to do.
"How can I cause myself to escape from this suffering?
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having heard the words of the devaputra Sunirmita, was greatly astonished;
he contemplated them with focused attention.
"What kind of bodies in the seven evil destinies will this Well-Established (Susthitamati) receive?
He then sat in stillness for a moment and focused his mind in contemplation;
he immediately saw that Well-Established was to receive the bodies of the seven evil destinies seven times over.
That is to say, they take on the bodies of pigs,
dogs, jackals, monkeys, pythons, snakes, crows, vultures, and the like;
they consume all manner of foul, evil, and impure things.
At that time, Śakra beheld the devaputra Susthita about to fall into the bodies of the sevenfold evil destinies;
he was deeply moved by compassion, and his grief and distress pierced through both body and mind.
He reflected deeply: "What plan should I devise? To whom may I turn for refuge?
Who is able to protect me so that I may escape this suffering?
Then he further thought: "Only the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—the Great Compassionate Father—is capable of this."
"How might I cause him to dwell securely and escape this suffering?
Having had this thought, Śakra, during the first watch of the night, adorned himself with various flowers and exquisite celestial garments.
Carrying flowers and incense, he went to the Jeta Grove,
approached the Blessed One, and paid him respectful homage;
having prostrated at his feet and circumambulated him seven times, he stood before him.
Kneeling with palms joined, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The Devaputra Sunirmita heard a voice declare that seven days hence his life would end,
and he would undergo seven successive rebirths in the miserable realms of the animal world."
Having heard these words, he was filled with extreme grief and suffering that pierced his heart.
"The World-Honored One is greatly compassionate and seeks our benefit;
how may we be delivered from this suffering?"
At that time, having heard these words,
the World-Honored One smiled and emitted various rays of light from the crown of his head,
which illuminated the trichiliocosm and returned to the Buddha’s presence.
If the Buddha, the World-Honored One, speaks of past events, light enters through his back;
if he speaks of future events, light enters through his chest;
if he speaks of matters concerning the hells, light enters through the soles of his feet.
If he speaks of matters concerning animals, light enters through the heels;
if he speaks of matters concerning hungry ghosts, light enters through the toes;
if he speaks of matters concerning humans, light enters through the knees.
If he speaks of the deeds of a Cakravartin King of Power, the light enters through the palm of his left hand;
if he speaks of the deeds of a Universal Monarch (Cakravartin), the light enters through the palm of his right hand;
if he speaks of celestial matters, the light enters through his navel.
If he speaks of the matters concerning śrāvakas, the light enters through his mouth;
if he speaks of the matters concerning pratyekabuddhas, the light enters between his eyebrows;
if he speaks of the matters concerning anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, the light enters through the crown of his head.
At that time, the light returned to where the Buddha was,
circled him three times, and entered through the Buddha’s mouth.
Then the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, saying:
O Lord of Devas, there is a dhāraṇī called the "Exalted and Victorious Uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgata," which is able to purify all the sufferings of the miserable realms and the cycle of birth and death.
Furthermore, it can purify and eliminate the sufferings of all hell realms, the realm of King Yama, and the animal kingdom;
moreover, it destroys all karma leading to the hells and causes one to turn toward the auspicious paths.
O Lord of Devas, this Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī possesses inconceivable and great supernatural power;
if there should be anyone by whom it is but once heard through the ear, [it shall bring about their liberation].
All evil karma created in previous lives shall be completely extinguished.
One shall obtain a pure, supreme, and wondrous body,
and wherever one is born, one will remember and never forget.
From one buddha-field to another buddha-field;
from one celestial realm to another celestial realm,
even traveling throughout the entirety of the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
One will remember and not forget the places where one is born.
Furthermore, O Lord of Devas, if a person is about to die,
by recollecting this dhāraṇī for even a moment, they shall regain an increased lifespan.
Their body, speech, and mind will be pure and free from suffering;
according to their merit and benefit, they shall all receive peace and security,
and they shall also be gazed upon by all Tathāgatas.
All celestial deities shall constantly serve as his guardians;
he will be revered by all people, and all evil obstacles will be eliminated.
All Bodhisattvas shall likewise provide him with protection and shelter.
If there are men or women who,
for even a brief moment, read, recite, and uphold this dhāraṇī,
you should know that all the sufferings of the three evil realms belonging to such persons [shall be extinguished].
They are destroyed and annihilated without remainder.
The pure lands of all Buddhas, the celestial palaces of all devas,
and the profound practices and vows of all Bodhisattvas— [all these are likewise destroyed].
They enter and roam at will, entirely without obstruction.
At that time, Śakra was single-mindedly eager to hear.
Then the Bhagavān observed the thoughts in Śakra’s mind.
With a mind of great compassion, he spoke this dhāraṇī method.
He then recited the mantra, saying:
Namo bhagavate.
Dhṛtarāṣṭraprativiśiṣṭabuddhabhagavatī.
Tadyathā oṃ viśuddha-tva-samantāpabhāsa-prabha.
Nāgavikrāntasvaprabhāsita-saṃdṛṣṭam-anuttarabodhibhājana.
Amṛtaviśuddhā hara hara kṣudrān vaśīkuru.
Sudhaye sudhaye gagana-viśuddhe uṣṇīṣe.
Vīrya-śuddhe sahasraraśmi-sandhite.
Sarva-tathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite mucye (mucye) svāhā.
Vajrakāyasamghanāścite sarvakavaraṇaviśodhite.
Pratiniṣṭhāpya āyoṣṭe samayādhiṣṭhe.
Mani mani mama mani tattvabuddha guṭi pariśuddhe.
Bhiḥ sphuṭa bhuvi śvete śye śye bhi śye bhi śye.
Samara samara sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhita śānte.
Vajre vajra-āveśa vajraprabha vadatu mama amuka-nāmnaḥ sarvasattvānāñca rakṣaya viśodhaya.
Sarvagate pariśuddhe sarvatathāgatasamavasaraṇe ātiṣṭha tiṣṭha.
Buddha buddha sambhārapariśuddhe.
*Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā svāhā*.

Although this mantra has been translated and transmitted by many, its phonology and orthography were not entirely perfect; therefore, it has been re-examined against the Sanskrit original and meticulously finalized. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
He addressed Śakra, saying: "This dhāraṇī-seal is named the *Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-uṣṇīṣavijaya-dhāraṇī-vidhi*.
It is also capable of eliminating all obstacles such as sinful karma."
O Lord of Devas, this dhāraṇī can purify all the sufferings of the defiled evil realms;
it has been [proclaimed] by eighty-eight hundred-thousand-koṭi-gaṅgā-sand numbers of Buddhas.
Together they shall proclaim, rejoice in, and uphold this,
sealing it with the wisdom-seal of the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana,
in order to shatter the net of the three evil destinies for all sentient beings.
It is for the sake of bringing liberation to all sentient beings within the realms of the hells, the animal kingdom, and the domain of King Yama;
and so that those beings oppressed by manifold sufferings who have fallen into the ocean of birth and death may attain liberation.
Furthermore, it causes those beings who are short-lived, of meager merit, and currently without protection,
as well as those sentient beings who delight in creating defiled and evil karma, to obtain benefit;
for this dhāraṇī possesses the power to sustain and uphold [beings] within Jambudvīpa.
Furthermore, it causes those with wrong views who do not believe in good and evil to wander through the various births and deaths within the three miserable realms, suffering in affliction;
beings of meager merit thus lose their way on the correct path.
All such beings as these shall receive benefit without exception;
they shall all be liberated from the heavy burden of manifold sufferings.
The Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of Devas: "I now proclaim this dhāraṇī and entrust it to you."
"You should bestow this upon the Devaputra Susthitamati,
so that he may receive, uphold, read, recite, and contemplate it;
and with love, respect, and offerings, he should remember and hold it fast without forgetting."
It shall also cause all sentient beings within Jambudvīpa to widely proclaim and disseminate this dhāraṇī, bringing immeasurable benefit;
it is likewise for the sake of all the sons of gods.
I have proclaimed this Great Dharani Seal and entrusted it to you.
O Lord of Devas, you should maintain it with correct mindfulness;
exert yourself in its protection so that it is not lost or forgotten.
Furthermore, O Lord of Devas,
if there should be anyone who hears this dhāraṇī for even a moment,
the sins of heavy obstructions and evil karma accumulated over a thousand kalpas will be [extinguished].
One should undergo various cycles of birth and death within the realms of hell-beings,
hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama,
as well as among the bodies of asuras, yakṣas, and spirits.
Pūtana, kaṭapūtana, apasmāra;
those with the bodies of mosquitoes, gadflies, tortoises, dogs, pythons, snakes, and so forth;
all birds and all fierce beasts.
All sentient beings, down to the bodies of ants,
shall no longer undergo further rebirth but will instead attain immediate transformation.
All the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and Bodhisattvas in their final birth before Buddhahood will assemble together in one place.
Or they may be born into a family of great Brahmin lineage,
or be born into the Kṣatriya caste, or into a noble, most eminent, and wealthy family.
O Lord of Devas, such as these are the types of persons.
Those who are born in such superior realms do so entirely because they have heard this dhāraṇī;
wherever they are born, they shall all obtain a pure, sublime, and wondrous body.
"O Devendra, such fruits of retribution, up to the most supreme state of bodhi,
all arise from praising the extraordinary merits of this dhāraṇī.
O Devendra, this dhāraṇī is named 'Auspicious' (Śrī)."
Why is this? Because it is able to eliminate all three evil realms.
This Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-vijayā-dhāraṇī is like the jewel-treasure of the Sun-store.
It is pure and free from blemish, like empty space;
its radiant flames shine through, pervading everywhere without exception.
It is likewise for all sentient beings who maintain this dhāraṇī with a pure mind.
It is like fine gold— bright, pure, and supple—
which brings joy to those who behold it and is not defiled by filth;
it is also like a lotus flower, which is not stained by falling dust.
It is the same for a celestial king who upholds this dhāraṇī:
by means of these pure karmas, he will surely be reborn in a happy realm.
Celestial King, wherever this dhāraṇī is present, in that place...
If one can thus copy, receive and uphold,
hear, praise, recite, respect, and make offerings to it,
all evil realms will be completely purified.
The sufferings of all hells will be swiftly extinguished. O Lord of Devas,
if there are men or women who write down this dhāraṇī and place it atop a high banner, [the benefits shall be as follows].
Whether placed upon a high mountain,
set within a multi-storied pavilion, or even enshrined within a stūpa—
O Lord of Devas, if there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or sons and daughters of noble family;
One may at times see the aforementioned banners and so forth from afar,
or be near them such that their shadows fall upon one's body,
or again, the dhāraṇīs and other [mantras] may be wafted by the wind.
O Śakra, Lord of Devas, as for those light particles of dust that fall upon the bodies [of beings],
the karmic offenses of those sentient beings would otherwise cause them to fall into the evil destinies of the hells, the hungry ghosts, or the animals.
In the realm of King Yama,
they do not undergo the sufferings of the asura bodies;
nor are they defiled by the stains of sin.
"O Devānām-indra, all these sentient beings have received the prediction of enlightenment from all the Buddhas;
they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
O Lord of Devas, how much more so if one further uses various flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense,
banners, pennants, flower canopies, robes, and necklaces,
and performs all manner of music and various adornments?
Construct a stūpa at a crossroads,
enshrine the dhāraṇī therein, and with palms joined in reverence,
circumambulate it clockwise while taking refuge and prostrating.
O Lord of Devas, those who can make such offerings as these are called mahāsattvas;
they are truly the sons of the Buddha and the pillars who uphold the Dharma.
Furthermore, this is a stūpa containing the entire body relics of the Tathāgata.
At that time, during the first watch of the night, Yama, the Dharma King, came to the place where the Buddha was,
bringing various exquisite garments and various flowers and incenses.
With powdered incense, scented ointments, sandalwood, and aloeswood,
they reverently made offerings and circumambulated the Buddha seven times;
having prostrated at his feet, they spoke these words:
I have heard the Tathāgata expound the dharma of the Great Power Dhāraṇī,
praising its inconceivable merit for those who uphold it.
World-Honored One, with great compassion, you take pity on and benefit sentient beings afflicted by the suffering of their transgressions.
"Blessed One, I shall constantly follow and protect [this person],
ensuring that the holder does not fall into hell;
for they have followed the Tathāgata’s instructions and protected me with mindfulness."
At that time, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Guardians of the World, circumambulated the Buddha three times and stood to one side.
They addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
"We only pray that the Tathāgata will once again extensively expound the dharma of the dhāraṇī for us.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Four Great Heavenly Kings, saying:
Listen attentively, for I shall explain to you the method for upholding this dhāraṇī;
I shall also explain it for the sake of all sentient beings with short lifespans.
If one wishes to receive and uphold [this practice], one should bathe for purification and don new, clean garments.
Beginning from the first day of the waxing moon until the full moon on the fifteenth day,
one should maintain the precepts with single-minded devotion and recite the dhāraṇī one thousand times.
It causes those of short lifespan to have their lives extended and restored, forever freeing them from the suffering of illness.
It is able to completely eliminate all karmic obstructions,
as well as all the sufferings of the hells and of all birds, beasts, and indeed all living beings.
If the sound of this dhāraṇī is heard even once by the ear, one shall exhaust this present body and never again undergo any further suffering.
The Buddha said: "Furthermore, if there should be someone who suddenly encounters a malignant illness and is oppressed by manifold sufferings..."
Those who hear this dhāraṇī shall immediately and forever be free from all evil diseases and the various sufferings thereof, which will be extinguished;
even those destined for rebirth in the evil realms shall attain liberation.
One shall immediately attain rebirth in the world of Abhirati;
after this present body has perished, one will never again receive a body born from a womb,
but shall be born by transformation within lotus flowers wherever one may be.
Wherever they are born, they will always attain the recollection of their past lives and maintain it without forgetting.
The Buddha said: "Furthermore, if there is a person who has previously committed all manner of extremely grave karmas and then immediately passes away..."
Due to these evil karmas, one should fall into hell;
or fall into the realms of animals, the domain of King Yama, or the destiny of hungry ghosts;
even unto falling within the *naraka* hells.
Whether they have been born in the water or have taken on various bodies as birds or beasts,
take a portion of the deceased's bones and a handful of pure earth,
and recite the dhāraṇī over them twenty-one times.
Scatter [the ashes] upon the bones;
the deceased will be reborn in heaven.
The Buddha said: "If a person can constantly recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times every day..."
One should accept all the supreme offerings of the world;
by relinquishing the body, one will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
If one constantly recites and contemplates [this], one's lifespan will further increase and one will experience all manner of happiness.
After casting off this body, they will immediately attain rebirth in various subtle and wondrous Buddha-fields.
They shall always assemble in one place together with all Buddhas,
and all Tathāgatas will constantly expound for them the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
All Buddhas bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment;
their bodies radiate light that illuminates all buddha-fields,
until they finally attain unsurpassed nirvana.
Furthermore, if one wishes to recite this dhāraṇī rite,
one should first take pure earth before the Buddha to construct an altar;
it should be made square, according to its intended size.
Scatter various kinds of grasses and flowers upon the altar,
burn all manner of famous incenses, place both knees on the ground or occasionally squat,
and with a mind constantly mindful of the Buddha, perform the mudrā of the *mūrdha-dhāraṇī*.
First, bend the index finger and press it with the thumb;
then, join the palms at the heart and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
Within that maṇḍala, like a king of clouds raining down various flowers,
one is able to universally make offerings to eighty-eight koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā River.
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, all praised him together, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! This is truly rare; you are indeed a son of the Buddha.
You have realized the samādhi of unobstructed wisdom and the samādhi of the adornment of the bodhicitta."
"Those who uphold this dhāraṇī should act in this manner.
The Buddha said, "Devendra, by means of my skillful expedients (*upāya-kauśalya*),
if there are any sentient beings who ought to fall into hell, I shall cause them to be liberated immediately."
All evil realms shall likewise be purified, extinguished without remainder.
Furthermore, it shall cause the lifespan of those who uphold it to increase.
O Lord of Devas, you should now take up this dharani method of mine.
He bestowed it upon the Devaputra Susthita,
commanding him: "After you have completed seven days of recitation,
you and Susthita shall come together to see me."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, personally received the dharma of the dhāraṇī from before the World-Honored One;
having upheld and recollected it, he returned to his own palace.
It was bestowed upon the Devaputra Susthita.
At that time, having received this dharani method,
the Devaputra Susthita maintained it according to the rite for six days and six nights, whereby all his aspirations were fulfilled.
First, one should undergo all the sufferings of the evil realms and be immediately liberated; then,
abiding in the factors of enlightenment, one’s lifespan is increased,
and immeasurable meritorious deeds gather like clouds at the appropriate time.
Filled with immeasurable joy, he cried out in a loud voice:
"How rare it is that the Tathāgata has preached this wondrous Dharma!
How rare it is that such clear verification is so exceedingly great and beyond measure!"
"The Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One is able to speak this divine mantra for us and for all sentient beings,
so that we may be liberated from the sufferings of the evil realms.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, waited until the seventh day had passed.
Together with the divine son Sunirmita and the host of devas,
they were adorned with flower garlands and carried exquisite incense, precious banners, streamers, canopies, celestial robes, and necklaces— subtle and wondrous ornaments.
Having approached the Buddha and performed offerings,
they presented the World-Honored One with celestial fine garments and various necklaces,
and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times.
Leaping for joy, he sat to one side,
gazing upon the Honored One’s countenance with eyes that never once left him.
At that time, the World-Honored One extended his golden-hued arm.
Then, with his right hand— adorned with the marks of a hundred merits, complete in all its characteristics, and fearless—
he stroked the crown of the crown prince’s head,
preached the Dharma for him, and bestowed upon him the prediction of awakening.
The Buddha told the Devaputra Sthira:
"This dhāraṇī-seal is named the 'Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī for Purifying All Evil Destinies.
You should receive and uphold it."
At that time, the Devaputra Susthita, Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
and the entire great assembly of all the devas who had gathered,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Buddha-Spoken Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī.
